summary: Jason argues the Cursor acquisition is highly accretive to SpaceX's IPO story, with complementary compute and coding AI positioning SpaceX/xAI to lead the coding leaderboard within 12 months, at a $2T IPO valuation target.
quote: I predict that this is going to move SpaceX, xAI, and Cursor to the front of the coding leaderboard within 12 months. That's my prediction.

summary: Chamath argues SpaceX is effectively acquiring Cursor at a ~50% discount via stock at a $2T valuation, getting valuable coding IP, training data, and a top-tier team — a smart jiu-jitsu move that turns excess Colossus GPU capacity into a competitive AI coding position.
quote: He can issue $60 billion of stock at a $2 trillion valuation and get a model and a service that I think is extremely compelling in coding... He gets all of that, and then he gets a very crack team... So I think it was a really good deal,

summary: Sacks views the SpaceX-Cursor deal as highly complementary: Cursor brings coding strength, enterprise clients, and training data, while xAI provides compute and a foundation model, accelerating xAI's competitive position in the hottest AI segment.
quote: Cursor brings to xAI the training data, a lot of enterprise clients, and the experience in coding. And I think this will accelerate xAI in this area.

summary: Jason sees Cursor as a money-printing machine with $2B ARR run rate tripling to $6B by end of 2026, and the SpaceX deal as highly value-accretive, resolving its compute constraints and positioning it at the top of the coding leaderboard.
quote: Cursor's run rate, $2 billion at the end of February. This is a money printing machine. They expect to end 2026 with a $6 billion run rate. They're going to triple it.

summary: Sacks suggests Salesforce may be a bargain at current valuations, citing Benioff's track record of successfully navigating every prior tech wave and his headless/agentic product pivot as reasons to believe he'll make AI work in Salesforce's favor.

summary: Friedberg acknowledges Salesforce is trading at less than 10x free cash flow — 'unbelievable' — and sees Benioff's headless/agentic product move as smart and potentially differentiating, but notes the broader SaaS deflation threat to cash flows.
quote: Salesforce today is down 9%, $140 billion enterprise value on $15 billion of free cash flow. This thing is trading at less than 10 times free cash flow. It's unbelievable.

summary: Chamath argues Salesforce looks historically cheap at 10x FCF but warns that AI-driven deflation of SaaS cash flows could compress multiples to 3–5x FCF regardless of business quality, making the bottom unclear.
